explanation: `create_before_destroy = true` tells Terraform to provision the replacement resource before tearing down the current one, avoiding a gap in availability [c:5173ec833c69]. Without it, the default order is destroy-then-create.

`ignore_changes` takes a list of attribute names that Terraform should not attempt to reconcile, so it will leave `desired_capacity` at whatever value the auto-scaler set [c:5cd7732a9c55]. `create_before_destroy` only affects replacement order, and `prevent_destroy` blocks deletions, neither of which is the issue here.

`ignore_changes` tells Terraform not to reconcile the listed attributes [c:8df2a85eeeec]. Even though the config value differs from the real resource, Terraform will not plan any action for that attribute. The wrong option — showing a replacement — would only happen without `ignore_changes`.
